name: Power iteration for a dominant eigenvector
definition: For real symmetric A and nonzero x₀, iterate x_(k+1)=Ax_k/||Ax_k||₂; estimate λ_k=x_kᵀAx_k/(x_kᵀx_k).
variables: A symmetric matrix; x_k iterate; λ_k Rayleigh quotient
assumptions: Unique eigenvalue of strictly largest nonzero magnitude, nonzero initial projection onto its eigenspace, direction convergence up to sign.
limitations: Slow for close eigenvalue magnitudes; does not determine the full spectrum.
failure_conditions: Zero matrix-vector product or absent dominant component
computation: Normalize matrix-vector products and check eigenpair residual.

name: Fixed-shift inverse iteration
definition: For real symmetric A and fixed shift μ outside its spectrum, solve (A−μI)y_k=x_k and set x_(k+1)=y_k/||y_k||₂.
variables: A symmetric matrix; μ fixed shift; x_k normalized iterate; y_k intermediate solve
assumptions: Unique closest eigenvalue to μ, nonzero starting projection, stable shifted linear solve.
limitations: Potentially ill-conditioned shifted system; direction may change sign.
failure_conditions: Singular shifted matrix or absent target component
computation: Factor shifted matrix once, solve repeatedly, normalize and check eigenpair residual.

name: Rayleigh quotient iteration
definition: For unit x_k and real symmetric A, let μ_k=x_kᵀAx_k; solve (A−μ_k I)y_k=x_k and set x_(k+1)=y_k/||y_k||₂ unless an eigenpair residual stop condition holds.
variables: A symmetric matrix; μ_k adaptive shift; y_k shifted solution; x_k normalized iterate
assumptions: Local convergence near a simple eigenvector, nonsingular shifted system unless already converged.
limitations: Repeated factorization; near singularity requires careful residual and solve handling; no guarantee of selecting prescribed eigenpair.
computation: Evaluate Rayleigh quotient and residual; solve shifted system and normalize if not converged.
